topic: Putting my newborn son to sleep
brief: A lullaby for my newborn son: soft, gentle and calm.
title: Lights Out, Little Man
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Yo, listen up, little man, it's lights out, no cap,
you been screaming all night, give your mama a break,
quit flexing them lungs, nobody's impressed,
shut them eyes, lock it down, get some rest.

[Chorus]
Lights out, little man, for real this time,
lights out, little man, you're wasting my grind,
lights out, little man, don't start that again,
lights out, little man, I'm counting to ten.

[Verse 2]
Your daddy's knocked out and the dog is too,
the whole block's sleeping, what's wrong with you,
I love you to bits, you know that's facts,
now hit the pillow and just relax.

[Chorus]
Lights out, little man, for real this time,
lights out, little man, you're wasting my grind,
lights out, little man, don't start that again,
lights out, little man, I'm counting to ten.
reason: On topic and fluent, but aggressive street slang ('no cap', 'quit flexing', 'shut them eyes') is the wrong register for a soft, gentle lullaby.
